summary_findings: Literary Tamil carries the whole 27-nakshatra system in Tamil phonology — the Tamil Lexicon prints the canonical list under நட்சத்திரம் as acuviṉi, paraṇi, kārttikai, urōkiṇi … irēvati (Tamil Lexicon, s.v. நட்சத்திரம், p. 2135) — and the twelve month-names still in daily use (Cittirai, Vaikāci, Āṉi, Āṭi, Āvaṇi, Puraṭṭāci, Aippaci, Kārttikai, Mārkaḻi, Tai, Māci, Paṅkuṉi) are asterism-derived, the Lexicon deriving Aippaci < āśvayuj, Puraṭṭāci < proṣṭhapadā, Mārkaḻi < mārgaśīrṣa, Paṅkuṉi < Pkt. phagguṇi, Vaikāci < vaiśākha, Āvaṇi < śrāvaṇa, Āṭi < āṣāḍha, Tai < taiṣī, Māci < māgha. That layer is recorded here compactly; the substance of this file is the layer that is not Sanskrit. Two Tamil word-classes generate indigenous star-names. The first is மீன் mīṉ 'star' — a Dravidian word the Lexicon derives from மின்னு- 'to flash' (DEDR 4876, with Ma. mīn, Ko./To. mi·n, Ka. mīn, Kur. bīnkō 'star'), homophonous but not identical with mīṉ 'fish' (DEDR 4885); the Lexicon's derivation of the fish-word from Sanskrit mīna is the older view that the Dravidian Etymological Dictionary does not follow. Counting compounds in -mīṉ name asterisms by their star-counts: அறுமீன் aṟumīṉ and ஆறாமீன் āṟāmīṉ 'six-star' = the Pleiades, எழுமீன் eḻumīṉ 'seven-star' = the Great Bear (Naṟṟiṇai 231), மும்மீன் mummīṉ 'three-star' = Mṛgaśīrṣa, ஐம்மீன் aimmīṉ 'five-star' = Hasta, with கடைமீன் kaṭaimīṉ 'last star' = Revatī and ஆதிமீன் ātimīṉ 'first star' = Aśvinī closing the circle from both ends. Descriptive -mīṉ compounds name the bright wanderers by colour and place: வெண்மீன் veṇmīṉ 'white star' and வெள்ளி veḷḷi 'the silver/white one' = Venus, செம்மீன் cemmīṉ 'red star' = Mars (and, disputed, Arundhatī and Ārdrā), மைம்மீன் maimmīṉ 'black star' = Saturn, வடமீன் vaṭamīṉ 'northern star' and சிறுமீன் ciṟumīṉ 'small star' = Arundhatī/Alcor, வால்மீன் vālmīṉ 'tail-star' = comet, வீழ்மீன் vīḻmīṉ 'falling star' = meteor, கோண்மீன் kōṇmīṉ 'seizing star' = planet as against நாண்மீன் nāṇmīṉ 'day-star' = lunar mansion. The second class is நாள் nāḷ 'day', which by itself means 'lunar asterism' already in the Tolkāppiyam, and which forms a full parallel set of asterism-names by translating the presiding deity into Tamil: எரிநாள் eri-nāḷ 'fire-star' = Kārttikai (the Sanskrit Āgneya), காற்றினாள் kāṟṟiṉāḷ 'wind-star' = Svātī/Arcturus (Sanskrit Vāyavya), நீர்நாள் nīr-nāḷ 'water-star' = Pūrāṭam, மருத்துவநாள் maruttuva-nāḷ 'physician-star' = Aśvinī, மதிநாள் mati-nāḷ 'moon-star' = Mṛgaśīrṣa, மாரிநாள் māri-nāḷ 'rain-star' and கதிர்நாள் katir-nāḷ 'sun-ray star' = Uttiram — and two formations with no Sanskrit model at all: நடுநாள் naṭu-nāḷ 'middle star' for Cittirai, the fourteenth of twenty-seven, and காற்றுமுந்துநாள் kāṟṟu-muntu-nāḷ 'the star that the wind-star precedes' for Viśākhā, an asterism named purely by its position in the Tamil sequence. Nine of the names collected here are attested in the Caṅkam corpus itself, verified verbatim against Project Madurai e-texts: veḷḷi in the drought-omen formula of Puṟanāṉūṟu 35, 117 and 388, veṇmīṉ in the opening couplet of Paṭṭiṉappālai, maimmīṉ and tūmam beside veḷḷi in Puṟanāṉūṟu 117, eḻumīṉ in Naṟṟiṇai 231, aṟumīṉ in Naṟṟiṇai 202, vaṭamīṉ in Puṟanāṉūṟu 122 and Kalittokai 2, ciṟumīṉ in Perumpāṇāṟṟuppaṭai 303, cemmīṉ in Patiṟṟuppattu 31 and Puṟanāṉūṟu 60, kōṇmīṉ in Ciṟupāṇāṟṟuppaṭai 242, nāṇmīṉ in Kalittokai 104, and vaikuṟumīṉ in Akanāṉūṟu 17. The Caṅkam sky is a sky of omens and seasons rather than of horoscopes: Venus quitting its proper northern station for the south is the standard figure for drought and misrule, and Puṟanāṉūṟu 117 stacks Saturn smoking, a comet appearing, and Venus running south as three portents that a good king's land survives. One genuine indigenous constellation-figure surfaced: Nacciṉārkkiṉiyar, glossing மகவெண்மீன் maka-veṇmīṉ at Paṭṭiṉappālai 35, says the Magha asterism 'has the shape of a bent yoke' (முடநுகம்போன்ற வடிவம்) — the Sickle of Leo seen as a crooked ox-yoke. Two names are seamen's and cultivators' rather than literary: ஆறாமீனறவோட்டு āṟāmīṉ-aṟavōṭṭu, the sun's passage through the Pleiades segment, 'regarded by seamen as a period when rough weather is to be anticipated', and ஐப்பசிக்குழப்பம் aippaci-k-kuḻappam, the north-east monsoon squall of the month named for Aśvinī. The Milky Way has a Tamil name of its own that is not a Ganges-metaphor: மாசு mācu, 'the stain', and its compound பூராடமாசு pūrāṭa-mācu, 'the Pūrāṭam stain' — the galaxy named for the Sagittarius asterism where it is brightest — beside the calque பால்வீதிமண்டலம் pāl-vīti-maṇṭalam 'milk-street region'. NEGATIVE FINDINGS, which matter as much: no Tamil name for SIRIUS was found anywhere in the Tamil Lexicon, Winslow or Fabricius — searches on 'Sirius', 'dog star', 'Lubdhaka' and 'Canis' return nothing astronomical, and the Sanskrit Mṛgavyādha/Lubdhaka has no Tamil reflex in the lexica; no Tamil name for ANTARES as an individual star, only Kēṭṭai as 'the 18th nakṣatra, part of Scorpio'; no Tamil name for ORION'S BELT as a distinct three-star group, the 'three stars' of mummīṉ being the Sanskrit Mṛgaśīrṣa head-group; and the TOLKĀPPIYAM, contrary to what one might expect of the oldest Tamil grammar, reckons its six seasons (perumpoḻutu) and six times-of-day (ciṟupoḻutu) by landscape, weather and light — kār with mullai, kūtir midnight with kuṟiñci, vaikaṟai-viṭiyal with marutam, eṟpāṭu with neytal, vēṉil noon with pālai (Poruḷatikāram, Akattiṇaiyiyal 6-12) — and names no asterism in doing so; its only mention of mīṉ is a sandhi rule in the Eḻuttatikāram. The two European calques பெரியகரடி periya-karaṭi 'Great Bear' and சின்னக்கரடி ciṉṉa-k-karaṭi 'Little Bear' are marked 'Pond.' (Puducherry) in the Lexicon's Supplement and are recorded here precisely because they are late and localised, not indigenous.

entries.literal_meaning: 'the shining one', from miṉṉu- 'to flash, glitter'
entries.usage_note: The ordinary Tamil word for star from the Caṅkam period to the present, and the base of nearly every indigenous Tamil star-name. Winslow adds the colloquial மீன் முளைத்திருக்கிறது 'stars appear', marked 'Vulgar usage', and the proverb மதியை மீன் சூழ்ந்ததுபோல 'as the stars surround the moon'.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. மீன்¹, vol. VI p. 3214; quoting Tirukkuṟaḷ 1116
entries.quote: மீன்¹ mīṉ , n. < மின்னு-. [K. mīn.] 1. Star; நட்சத்திரம். பதியிற் கலங்கிய மீன் (குறள், 1116).
entries.notes: HOMONYM, the central one for this file. The Lexicon prints two separate headwords on the same page: மீன்¹ mīṉ 'star', derived from the Tamil verb மின்னு- 'to flash', and மீன்² mīṉ 'fish; Pisces of the zodiac; shark', which it derives from Sanskrit mīna. Burrow and Emeneau keep them apart on the same principle but treat both as Dravidian: DEDR 4876 gives Ta. miṉ 'flash, glitter, lightning' … mīṉ 'star', with Ma. mīn, Ko. mi·n, To. mi·n, Ka. mīn, Kur. bīnkō, Malt. bínḍke 'star'; DEDR 4885 gives Ta. mīṉ 'fish' with cognates in every Dravidian branch, i.e. the fish-word is not a Sanskrit loan either. The two are homophones of independent Dravidian origin. Every -mīṉ entry below therefore needs its astronomical sense shown from context, and the fish sense excluded; the Lexicon's own definitions do that here. Verified at https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/burrow_query.py?page=435 and .../burrow_query.py?page=436. Senses 2 and 3 of மீன்¹ also make the bare word a name for the 14th nakṣatra (Cittirai) and the 13th (Attam).

entries.usage_note: The standard modern Tamil word for a star, distinguishing it unambiguously from mīṉ 'fish'. The Lexicon records the colloquial contraction விம்மீன் vimmīṉ, marked 'Loc.'
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. விண்மீன், vol. VI p. 3665, citing the Cūṭāmaṇi Nikaṇṭu
entries.quote: விண்மீன் viṇ-mīṉ , n. < id. + மீன்¹. Star; நட்சத்திரம். (சூடா.)
entries.notes: Parallel formations with the same sense: வான்மீன்¹ vāṉ-mīṉ 'heaven-star' (p. 3626, from the aruñcolpporuḷ commentary on Puṟanāṉūṟu) and மோட்டுமீன் mōṭṭu-mīṉ (p. 3383, citing Cīvakacintāmaṇi 2325). வான்மீன்¹ must not be confused with வான்மீன்² = வால்மீன் 'comet' on the same page — the difference is வான் 'sky' against வால் 'tail'.

entries.usage_note: The commonest Tamil term for a lunar asterism, and the second element of the whole -nāḷ class of Tamil asterism-names recorded below. The semantic bridge is the day named by the asterism the moon is in.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. நாள் sense 7, vol. IV p. 2232; quoting Tolkāppiyam, Eḻuttatikāram 286
entries.quote: 7. Lunar asterism; நட்சத்திரம். திங்களு நாளு முந்துகிளந் தன்ன (தொல். எழுத். 286).
entries.notes: The Tolkāppiyam line quoted — 'as when the moon and the nāḷ were mentioned before' — puts the sense in the oldest surviving Tamil grammar. Sense 8 extends it to the lunar day, the period of the moon's passage through one asterism.

entries.usage_note: The Caṅkam term for the lunar mansions collectively, explicitly opposed by the Lexicon to கோண்மீன் kōṇmīṉ 'planet'. The Kalittokai image is of the moon ringed by the asterisms.
entries.citation: Kalittokai 104, l. 27 (Neytaṟkali); Project Madurai e-text PM 0221
entries.quote: நாள்மீன் வாய் சூழ்ந்த மதி போல், மிடை மிசைப்
entries.notes: The Project Madurai text prints நாள்மீன்; the Tamil Lexicon headword is நாண்மீன் (nasal assimilation) and cites this same line as கலித். 104, 27, glossing 'The lunar asterism; அசுவதி முதலிய நட்சத்திரப்பொது' (s.v. நாண்மீன், vol. IV p. 2212, https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/tamil-lex_query.py?qs=%E0%AE%A8%E0%AE%BE%E0%AE%A3%E0%AF%8D%E0%AE%AE%E0%AF%80%E0%AE%A9%E0%AF%8D&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact). The Lexicon also uses நாண்மீன் in its own Tamil definition of நட்சத்திரம், 'the twenty-seven nāṇmīṉ'.

entries.usage_note: The Tamil opposition between the wandering and the fixed lights: kōṇmīṉ 'planet' against nāṇmīṉ 'lunar mansion'. The Ciṟupāṇāṟṟuppaṭai simile is of the sun ringed by planets.
entries.citation: Ciṟupāṇāṟṟuppaṭai ll. 242-243; Project Madurai e-text PM 0064
entries.quote:
வாணிற விசும்பிற் கோண்மீன் சூழ்த்த
விளங்கதிர் ஞாயி றெள்ளூந் தோற்றத்து
entries.notes: The Tamil Lexicon (s.v. கோண்மீன், vol. II p. 1181) defines it 'Planet, dist. fr. nāṇ-mīṉ; கிரகம்' and cites this exact line as சிறுபாண். 242. Kalittokai 5 sets the two words side by side in one line, 'நாளும் கோள்மீன் தகைத்தலும் தகைமே' (PM 0221), with the fuller form கோள்மீன்.

entries.usage_note: Sanskrit uḍu in Tamil phonology, a learned word of the nikaṇṭus rather than of speech. Winslow glosses it simply 'A star, விண்மீன்'.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. உடு³, vol. I p. 399, citing the Piṅkala Nikaṇṭu
entries.quote: * உடு³ uṭu , n. < uḍu. Star; நட்சத்திரம். (பிங்.)
entries.notes: HOMONYM warning: the Lexicon prints six உடு headwords on the same page — 'ditch, moat', 'goat, sheep' (< huḍu), 'arrow, arrow-head, feather of an arrow, boatman's pole' (< huḍa), and a tree. Only உடு³ is astronomical, and the Lexicon marks it with an asterisk as a Sanskrit loan.

entries.usage_note: Sanskrit tārakā in Tamil form; the collective தாராகணம் tārā-kaṇam and தாரகாகணம் tārakā-kaṇam are the Tamil terms for a constellation or star-cluster.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. தாரகை¹, vol. III p. 1843; quoting Tirukkōvaiyār 116
entries.quote: தாரகை¹ tārakai , n. < tārakā. 1. Star; நட்சத்திரம். நாப்பண்வண் டாரகைபோல் (திருக்கோ. 116). 2. Apple of the eye; கண்மணி. (யாழ். அக.)
entries.notes: HOMONYM: sense 2 is 'apple of the eye', and தாரகை² is 'earth'. For 'constellation, cluster of stars' the Lexicon gives தாராகணம் (p. 1844, quoting Nāṉmukaṉ Tiruvantāti 63) and தாரகாகணம் (p. 1843).

entries.usage_note: THE COMPACT RECORD OF THE SANSKRITIC LAYER. This one entry carries the canonical Tamil forms of all 27 nakshatras as the Tamil Lexicon prints them, so that the rest of this file can be spent on names that are not Sanskrit.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. நட்சத்திரம் sense 2, vol. IV p. 2135
entries.quote: 2. (Astron.) Lunar constellation, 27 in number, viz., acuviṉi, paraṇi, kārttikai, urōkiṇi, mirukacīriṭam, tiruvātirai, puṉarpūcam, pūcam, āyiliyam, makam, pūram, uttiram, astam, cittirai, cuvāti, vicākam, aṉuṣam, kēṭṭai, mūlam, pūrāṭam, uttirāṭam, tiruvōṇam, aviṭṭam, cataiyam, pūraṭṭāti, uttiraṭṭāti, irēvati; அசுவனி, பரணி, கார்த்திகை, உரோகிணி, மிருகசீரிடம், திருவாதிரை, புனர்பூசம், பூசம், ஆயிலியம், மகம், பூரம், உத்திரம், அஸ்தம், சித்திரை, சுவாதி, விசாகம், அனுஷம், கேட்டை, மூலம், பூராடம், உத்திராடம், திருவோணம், அவிட்டம், சதையம், பூரட்டாதி, உத்திரட்டாதி, இரேவதி என்னும் இருபத்தேழு நாண்மீன்.
entries.notes: Each of these is the corresponding Sanskrit nakshatra name in Tamil phonology, and each maps one-to-one onto an id in the Sanskrit database: acuviṉi = ashvini, paraṇi = bharani, kārttikai = krittika, urōkiṇi = rohini, mirukacīriṭam = mrigashirsha, tiruvātirai = ardra, puṉarpūcam = punarvasu, pūcam = pushya, āyiliyam = ashlesha, makam = magha, pūram = purva-phalguni, uttiram = uttara-phalguni, astam = hasta, cittirai = chitra, cuvāti = svati, vicākam = vishakha, aṉuṣam = anuradha, kēṭṭai = jyeshtha, mūlam = mula, pūrāṭam = purva-ashadha, uttirāṭam = uttara-ashadha, tiruvōṇam = shravana, aviṭṭam = dhanishtha, cataiyam = shatabhishaj, pūraṭṭāti = purva-bhadrapada, uttiraṭṭāti = uttara-bhadrapada, irēvati = revati. The Lexicon's own Tamil paraphrase calls them 'the twenty-seven nāṇmīṉ', i.e. it defines the Sanskrit term with the vernacular one. Individual Tamil entries elsewhere in the Lexicon locate several of them on the modern sky: அத்தம்⁸ attam 'the 13th nakṣatra, the constellation Corvus' (p. 65), அவிட்டம் aviṭṭam 'the 23rd nakṣatra, the constellation Dolphin' (p. 157), உரோகிணி urōkiṇi 'the 4th nakṣatra, Hyades, part of Taurus' (p. 453), திருவோணம் tiruvōṇam 'the 22nd nakṣatra, constellation of Aquila' (p. 1922), உத்தரட்டாதி uttaraṭṭāti 'the 26th nakṣatra, part of the constellations of Pegasus and Andromeda' (p. 407), திருவாதிரை tiruvātirai 'the 6th nakṣatra, part of Orion' (p. 1917), கேட்டை kēṭṭai 'the 18th nakṣatra, part of Scorpio' (p. 1092), அனுஷம் aṉuṣam 'the 17th nakṣatra, part of Scorpio' (p. 197), சித்திரை cittirai 'the 14th nakṣatra, part of Virgo' (p. 1391).

entries.usage_note: The indigenous Tamil name of the Pleiades, formed from ஆறு āṟu 'six' + mīṉ 'star', and attested in the Caṅkam corpus. It is the Tamil counting-name, independent of the Sanskrit Kṛttikā, though the Lexicon glosses it with கார்த்திகை.
entries.citation: Naṟṟiṇai 202, ll. 8-9 (Pālai, by Pālai Pāṭiya Peruṅkaṭuṅkō); Project Madurai e-text PM 0296
entries.quote:
கண்டிசின் வாழியோ குறுமகள் நுந்தை
அறுமீன் பயந்த அறம் செய் திங்கள்
entries.notes: The Tamil Lexicon (s.v. அறுமீன், vol. I p. 181, https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/tamil-lex_query.py?qs=%E0%AE%85%E0%AE%B1%E0%AF%81%E0%AE%AE%E0%AF%80%E0%AE%A9%E0%AF%8D&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact) defines it 'Pleiades, as containing six stars; கார்த்திகை. (பிங்.)', citing the Piṅkala Nikaṇṭu. The Naṟṟiṇai line joins the six stars to the moon — the Kārttikai full moon — and belongs to the Murugan birth-cycle: the Lexicon's அறுமீன்காதலன் aṟumīṉ-kātalaṉ (p. 181) is Skanda 'as one brought up by the goddesses of the Pleiades'. Winslow, s.v. அறு, gives the same word as 'The pleiades regarded as six stars being the third lunar constellation of the Hindus' and marks it '(p.)', poetical.

entries.usage_note: A second form of the counting-name, and the one that carries the seamen's compound below.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. ஆறாமீன், vol. I p. 259
entries.quote: ஆறாமீன் āṟā-mīṉ , n. < id. + id. +. Pleiades, as containing six stars; கார்த்திகை.
entries.notes: The Tamil tradition consistently counts six Pleiads, not seven as in the Sanskrit Kṛttikāḥ; hence the six presiding goddesses of கார்த்திகைத்தேவிமார் (p. 880) and வாகுலை (p. 3574).

entries.usage_note: A third Tamil counting-name for the Pleiades, from the same numeral ஆறு.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. அறுவாய்², vol. I p. 182; quoting Kallāṭam 90, 9
entries.quote: அறுவாய்² aṟu-vāy , n. < ஆறு³ +. The third nakṣatra, as consisting of six stars; கார்த்திகை. அறுவாய் நிறைந்த மதிப்புறத் தோவென (கல்லா. 90, 9).
entries.notes: HOMONYM: அறுவாய்¹ on the previous page, from அறு- 'to cut', means 'opening in a cut or wound' and 'vacant gap, as of the moon in its waxing phases' — and it is quoted from Tirukkuṟaḷ 1117 with the same collocation அறுவாய் நிறைந்த as the astronomical entry. The two senses can only be separated by context; here the moon is 'filled' beside the six stars.

entries.sky_object: the Pleiades / the third nakshatra / the eighth Tamil month
entries.usage_note: Sanskrit Kṛttikā in Tamil phonology — asterism, month, and the lamp-festival of the Kārttikai full moon in one word, and by far the most alive of the Sanskritic star-names in Tamil.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. கார்த்திகை, vol. II p. 880
entries.quote: கார்த்திகை kārttikai , n. < kṛttikā. 1. The constellation Pleiades, part of mēṭa-rāci and iṭapa-rāci; ஒரு நட்சத்திரம். (திவா.) 2. cf. kārttika. The eighth month of the Indian calendar; ஒரு மாதம். (சைவச. ஆசாரி. 79.) … 4. cf. kārttika. The full-moon day in the month of Kārttikai when every house is beautifully lit with lamps; கார்த்திகைமாதத்தில் வீடுதோறும் விளக்கேற்றிக் கொண்டாடும் பூர்ணிமை நாள்.
entries.notes: The lamp-festival is independently visible in the Caṅkam corpus: Naṭṭār's commentary on Akanāṉūṟu identifies the crowd of women raising lamps in a simile as the கார்த்திகை festival (Project Madurai PM 0490_01, https://www.projectmadurai.org/pm_etexts/utf8/pmuni0490_01.html). The Lexicon also has திருக்கார்த்திகை (p. 1897), 'a festival celebrated in the month of Kārttikai on the day when the moon is in conjunction with Pleiades'.

entries.sky_object: the sun's passage through the Pleiades (seasonal marker)
entries.literal_meaning: the running-through of the six stars
entries.usage_note: A SEAMEN'S TERM — the clearest surviving trace in the lexica of Tamil coastal star-reckoning. The Pleiades segment of the zodiac marks the season of dangerous weather for boats.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. ஆறாமீனறவோட்டு, vol. I p. 259, marked (W.) after Winslow
entries.quote: ஆறாமீனறவோட்டு āṟā-mīṉ-aṟa-v-ōṭṭu , n. < id. +. Passage of the sun through the segment of the Zodiac occupied by Pleiades, regarded by seamen as a period when rough weather is to be anticipated; கார்த்திகையில் சூரியன் பிரவேசிக்குங்காலம். (W.)
entries.notes: Winslow's own entry, s.v. ஆறு, is independent confirmation: 'The transit of the sun through the pleiades, regarded by seamen, as a critical or disastrous season, when rough weather is to be looked for' (A Comprehensive Tamil and English Dictionary, 1862, p. 76, https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/winslow_query.py?qs=Pleiades&matchtype=default). The season is the north-east monsoon; compare ஐப்பசிக்குழப்பம் below.

entries.usage_note: A Tamil name of the Pleiades recorded by the Tivākaram, of obscure motivation.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. இறால் sense 3, vol. I p. 363, citing the Tivākaram
entries.quote: இறால் iṟāl , n. prob. இறு¹-. 1. Shrimp, prawn, macroura; மீன்வகை. (பிங்.) 2. Bluish seer-fish, Cybium commersonii; வெள்ளிறால். 3. The third nakṣatra. See கார்த்திகை. (திவா.) 4. Bull; எருது. (பிங்.) 5. Honeycomb; தேன்கூடு.
entries.notes: HOMONYM, and a bad one: the same headword is 'shrimp', 'seer-fish', 'bull' and 'honeycomb'. Only the Tivākaram-sourced sense 3 is astronomical. Winslow independently records the sense — 'The third lunar mansion, the pleiades, கார்த்திகைநாள்' (1862, p. 113) — which is why it is kept, but the motivation of the name is unrecoverable and no literary attestation in the astronomical sense was found. Confidence 'likely' reflects the identification's dependence on two dictionaries with no verse behind them.

entries.sky_object: the six goddesses of the Pleiades
entries.usage_note: Sanskrit Vahulā (cf. Bahulā, a Sanskrit name of the Pleiades) in Tamil form, recorded from the Yāḻppāṇa Akarāti, the Jaffna Tamil dictionary.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. வாகுலை, vol. VI p. 3574, citing the Yāḻppāṇa Akarāti
entries.quote: வாகுலை vākulai , n. < Vahulā. The six presiding female deities of the Pleiades; அறு மீனாகிய கார்த்திகைப்பெண்கள். (யாழ். அக.)
entries.notes: The Lexicon's Tamil paraphrase uses அறுமீன் — 'the Kārttikai women who are the six stars' — so the Sanskritic name is defined by the vernacular one. Compare கார்த்திகைத்தேவிமார் (p. 880) and கார்த்திகைப்பெண்கள் (p. 880), the Tamil equivalents.

entries.usage_note: A Tamil translation, not a borrowing: the Sanskrit Āgneya 'belonging to Agni' rendered with the native Tamil words எரி 'fire' and நாள் 'asterism'.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. எரிநாள், vol. I p. 531, citing the Piṅkala Nikaṇṭu
entries.quote: எரிநாள் eri-nāḷ , n. < எரி +. The third nakṣatra. See கார்த்திகை. (பிங்.)
entries.notes: Beside it the Lexicon has the half-borrowed அங்கிநாள் aṅki-nāḷ (p. 22, < Skt. agni + Tamil nāḷ), 'the third nakṣatra' and also 'the thirteenth', and கனலிநாள் kaṉali-nāḷ (p. 836), 'fire-star' for the 13th. The Sanskrit database entry 'agneya' warns that Āgneya is Kṛttikā and not the star Agni; the same warning applies to eri-nāḷ.

modern_star.bayer: α, β, γ, δ, ε, ζ, η Ursae Majoris

entries.usage_note: The indigenous Tamil name of the Great Bear, from ஏழு ēḻu 'seven'. The Naṟṟiṇai simile — white sea-crows settling on the dark sea like the Seven Stars in a clear sky, 'in the manner of hands folded in worship' — shows the asterism was both named and venerated in Caṅkam Tamil.
entries.citation: Naṟṟiṇai 231, ll. 1-2 (Neytal, by Iḷanākaṉār); Project Madurai e-text PM 0296
entries.quote:
மை அற விளங்கிய மணி நிற விசும்பில்
கைதொழும் மரபின் எழு மீன் போல
entries.notes: The Tamil Lexicon (s.v. எழுமீன், vol. I p. 544, https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/tamil-lex_query.py?qs=%E0%AE%8E%E0%AE%B4%E0%AF%81%E0%AE%AE%E0%AF%80%E0%AE%A9%E0%AF%8D&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact) defines it 'The seven principal stars of Ursa Major, Charles's Wain; சப்தரிஷிமண்டலம்' and cites this exact line as நற். 231. The Sanskritic equivalent in Tamil is சத்தரிஷிமண்டலம் catta-riṣi-maṇṭalam (p. 1249), 'Ursa major or the Great Bear, the seven chief stars of which are personified as saptaṛṣi', and ஸப்தர்ஷிமண்டலம் (p. 3905).

entries.usage_note: A Tamil formation for the Great Bear conceived as the turning polar wheel; the commentary passage quoted makes it the reference circle against which the planets' positions are described.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. சுடர்ச்சக்கரம், vol. III p. 1502; quoting the commentary on Paripāṭal 19, 46
entries.quote: சுடர்ச்சக்கரம் cuṭar-c-cakkaram , n. < id. +. The Great Bear, polar circle; துருவசக்கரம். சுடர்ச்சக்கரத்தைப் பொருந்திவரும் ஆதித்தன் முதலாக வருங் கோட்களது நிலைமையை (பரிபா. 19, 46, உரை).
entries.notes: The Lexicon equates it with துருவசக்கரம் turuva-cakkaram (p. 1984), 'The wheel of Dhruva, turning the heavens and causing the diurnal motions', whose sense 2 is likewise 'Ursa major'. The name therefore hovers between the Bear itself and the whole polar circle it turns on; confidence 'likely' for the identification with Ursa Major specifically.

entries.usage_note: A LATE CALQUE, not indigenous: the European 'Great Bear' translated word for word into Tamil, recorded by the Lexicon's Supplement and marked 'Pond.', i.e. current at Pondicherry. Recorded here precisely so that it is not mistaken for old Tamil sky-lore.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon Supplement (University of Madras, 1939), s.v. பெரியகரடி, p. S372, marked Pond.
entries.quote: பெரியகரடி periya-karaṭi , n. < பெரு-மை +. The Great Bear; சப்தரிஷிமண்டலம். Pond.
entries.notes: Its pair சின்னக்கரடி ciṉṉa-k-karaṭi, 'The constellation Little Bear; ஒரு நக்ஷத்திரத்தொகுதி. Pond.' (Supplement p. S280), confirms the pattern: a bear-pair is a European constellation scheme, and the Tamil tradition otherwise counts these stars as seven ṛṣis or simply as eḻumīṉ 'the seven stars'. The French colonial context of Pondicherry is the obvious channel; the Lexicon does not say so and neither do I.

entries.usage_note: The standard Caṅkam figure for a wife's chastity — 'the lady of gentle words whose chastity is like the northern star'. The comparison is to a star that never leaves its place.
entries.citation: Puṟanāṉūṟu 122, l. 8 (by Kapilar, on Malaiyamāṉ Tirumuṭikkāri); Project Madurai e-text PM 0057
entries.quote: வடமீன் புரையுங் கற்பின், மடமொழி,
entries.notes: IDENTIFICATION DISPUTED. The Tamil Lexicon (s.v. வடமீன், vol. VI p. 3474, https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/tamil-lex_query.py?qs=%E0%AE%B5%E0%AE%9F%E0%AE%AE%E0%AF%80%E0%AE%A9%E0%AF%8D&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact) reads it as Arundhatī — its sense 1 refers to அருந்ததி sense 2, 'the scarcely visible star Alcor of the great Bear', and sense 2 to Arundhatī the wife of Vasiṣṭha — and cites this line. Winslow agrees: 'வடமீன், s. A small star in Ursa Major, as அருந்ததி' (1862, p. 912). But the name means simply 'northern star', and the chastity-simile would work as well for the pole star; readers who take வடமீன் as Dhruva are not obviously wrong, and the Lexicon itself glosses அருந்ததி only as 'the scarcely visible star Alcor'. Kalittokai 2 has the same formula independently — 'வடமீன் போல் தொழுது ஏத்த வயங்கிய கற்பினாள்' (PM 0221) — and there the star is worshipped, which again fits either. Marked disputed for that reason.

entries.usage_note: The strongest Caṅkam identification of Arundhatī, because the poet gives the star's position as well as its name: 'the small star that shines in the northern quarter of the great good sky'.
entries.citation: Perumpāṇāṟṟuppaṭai ll. 302-303 (by Kaṭiyalūr Uruttiraṅkaṇṇaṉār); Project Madurai e-text PM 0069
entries.quote:
பெருநல் வானத்து வடவயின் விளங்குஞ்
சிறுமீன் புரையுங் கற்பி னறுநுதல்
entries.notes: The Tamil Lexicon (s.v. சிறுமீன், vol. III p. 1463) gives '1. The star Arundhati; அருந்ததி' and cites this line as பெரும்பாண். 303. HOMONYM: sense 2 of the same headword is 'Loach', a fish — சிறுமீன் is equally 'small fish'; here the preceding line 'in the northern quarter of the great sky' excludes it. Confidence 'likely' rather than 'certain' because 'the small star in the north' is a description that fits Alcor best but is not a proper name pinning it.

modern_star.common_name: Alcor (also read as Mars, or as Betelgeuse)

entries.usage_note: One Tamil name with three competing referents in the Caṅkam corpus itself. In Patiṟṟuppattu 31 it is a chaste woman's exemplar 'foremost among the women who move in the sky', i.e. Arundhatī among the ṛṣis' wives; in Puṟanāṉūṟu 60 it is a red star twinkling in the high sky.
entries.citation: Patiṟṟuppattu 31, ll. 26-28 (Fourth Ten, by Kāppiyāṟṟuk Kāppiyaṉār); Project Madurai e-text PM 0038
entries.quote:
விசும்புவழங்கு மகளிர் உள்ளும் சிறந்த
செம்மீன் அனையள்நின் தொல்நகர்ச் செல்வி
entries.notes: IDENTIFICATION GENUINELY DISPUTED, and the Tamil Lexicon itself records all three readings under one headword (s.v. செம்மீன், vol. III p. 1598, https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/tamil-lex_query.py?qs=%E0%AE%9A%E0%AF%86%E0%AE%AE%E0%AF%8D%E0%AE%AE%E0%AF%80%E0%AE%A9%E0%AF%8D&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact): '1. The star Arundhati … (பதிற்றுப். 31, 28). 2. Mars; செவ்வாய். செம்மீ னிமைக்கு மாக விசும்பின் (புறநா. 60, 2). 3. The 6th nakṣatra. See திருவாதிரை. (புறநா. 60, 2, உரை.)' — i.e. the Puṟanāṉūṟu line is read as Mars by the Lexicon and as Ārdrā (Betelgeuse) by the old commentary on the same line. The Puṟanāṉūṟu 60 context, verified at PM 0057, is 'முந்நீர் நாப்பண் திமில்சுடர் போலச், / செம்மீன் இமைக்கும் மாக விசும்பின்' — 'in the high sky where the red star twinkles like a fishing-boat's lamp in mid-ocean'. All three candidates (Mars, Betelgeuse, Antares by colour) are red; Arundhatī is not, which is why sense 1 is best explained as the fixed epithet transferred. HOMONYM: sense 4 of the same headword is a sperm whale. sanskrit_db_id given as arundhati for the Patiṟṟuppattu sense; for the Puṟanāṉūṟu sense the candidates are the planet Mars (no Sanskrit-database entry) or 'ardra'.

entries.usage_note: A hybrid of the same idea as vaṭa-mīṉ, with the Sanskrit word for north. The Lexicon's definition is unusually precise about which star is meant.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. உத்தரமீன், vol. I p. 408; quoting Cētupurāṇam, Tuttamai 6
entries.quote: *உத்தரமீன் uttara-mīṉ , n. < id. +. The star Arundhati in Ursa Major, the smaller of the two in Mizar, the central star in the tail; அருந்ததி நக்ஷத்திரம். உத்தரமீனின் கொண்கன் (சேதுபு. துத்தம. 6).
entries.notes: 'The smaller of the two in Mizar, the central star in the tail' is an unambiguous description of Alcor beside Mizar, ζ Ursae Majoris. This is the one Tamil entry that fixes Arundhatī on the sky beyond doubt, and it retro-justifies the identification of vaṭamīṉ and ciṟumīṉ. Beside it the Lexicon has குலமீன் kula-mīṉ 'clan-star' = Arundhatī (p. 1023, quoting Kallāṭam 73, 1).

entries.usage_note: A name for Arundhatī used in one of the most striking sky-passages in the Caṅkam corpus: of the seven women dwelling by the shining banyan in the northern quarter, one — the divine star Cāliṉi — abstains, and the other six partake, and so become the Pleiades who bear Murugan.
entries.citation: Paripāṭal 5, ll. 43-45; Project Madurai e-text PM 0087
entries.notes: The Tamil Lexicon (s.v. சாலினி¹ sense 2, vol. III p. 1391) gives 'Wife of Vasiṣṭha. See அருந்ததி' and cites this exact line as பரிபா. 5, 44. It derives the word from Sanskrit śālinī. HOMONYM: சாலினி¹ sense 1 is a woman oracle possessed by a spirit (quoted from Cilappatikāram 12, 7), சாலினி² is a gourd and சாலினி³ a toddy-seller; only sense 2 is astronomical. Note the passage's own phrase கடவுள் ஒரு மீன், 'the one divine star' — Tamil mīṉ used of Arundhatī directly. Winslow s.v. சாலி also records 'A name of Arundhati … supposed to have become one of the stars in Ursa Major' (1862, p. 441). Confidence 'likely': the identification of Cāliṉi with Arundhatī rests on the commentarial tradition reported by the Lexicon rather than on anything in the verse itself.

entries.usage_note: Sanskrit Dhruva in Tamil phonology. No indigenous Tamil name for the pole star was found in either the Tamil Lexicon or Winslow — every Tamil term for it is built on this loan.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. துருவம் sense 4, vol. IV p. 1984, marked (W.) after Winslow
entries.quote: Pole Star; துருவநட்சத்திரம். (W.) 5. The pole of any great circle of the sphere, especially the celestial poles; பூசக்கர முனை. (W.)
entries.notes: NEGATIVE FINDING recorded here: searching the English side of the Lexicon for 'pole star' returns only Sanskrit-derived compounds — சிம்சுமாரசக்கரம் cimcumāra-cakkaram (p. 1422, < Śiṃśumāra, the Sanskrit celestial porpoise), துருவபதம், துருவமண்டலம், துருவன் 'the son of King Uttānapāda believed to have become the pole-star', நட்சத்திரநேமி — and no Tamil formation at all. The Śiṃśumāra figure enters Tamil too: சிம்சுமாரப்ரஜாபதி (Supplement p. S276), 'the region of the Pole Star beyond the nakṣatra-pada', quoted from a Vaiṣṇava commentary.

entries.usage_note: The Tamil form of Agastya, both the sage credited with the first Tamil grammar and the star of which he is the regent. The Lexicon's quotation is from the commentary on Paripāṭal and calls it plainly 'the star named Agastiyaṉ'.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. அகத்தியன் sense 2, vol. I p. 10; quoting the commentary on Paripāṭal 11, 11
entries.quote: 2. The star Canopus, of which Agastya is the regent; அகஸ்திய நக்ஷத்திரம். அகத்திய னென்னு மீன் உயர்ந்த தன்னிடத்தைக் கடந்து மிதுனத்தைப் பொருந்த (பரிபா. 11, 11, உரை).
entries.notes: The Lexicon also has the fully Sanskritic அகஸ்தியநட்சத்திரம் (p. 16), 'The star Canopus'. The commentary phrase அகத்தியன் என்னும் மீன் — 'the star called Akattiyaṉ' — again uses the Tamil word mīṉ for a named star.

entries.literal_meaning: the sage of the Potiyil hill
entries.usage_note: A TAMIL LOCALISATION of the Canopus-sage: Agastya named not by his Sanskrit name but by the southern Tamil mountain he is said to dwell on. The verse describes him cleaving the high ridge and reaching Gemini — the star's heliacal position in a datable sky-description.
entries.citation: Paripāṭal 11, ll. 11-12 (by Nallantuvaṉār); Project Madurai e-text PM 0087
entries.quote:
பொதியில் முனிவன் புரை வரைக் கீறி
மிதுனம் அடைய, விரி கதிர் வேனில்
entries.notes: The identification with Canopus is the commentary's, not the verse's: the Tamil Lexicon s.v. அகத்தியன் quotes the urai on this very line (பரிபா. 11, 11, உரை) as 'the star called Akattiyaṉ, passing beyond its high station, joining Gemini'. The mūlam text quoted here is verified independently at Project Madurai. The whole of Paripāṭal 11, ll. 1-12 is a sky-description with Venus in Aries (உருகெழு வெள்ளி வந்து ஏற்றியல் சேர, l. 4) and other planetary placements, so a star is what is meant. Confidence 'likely' because the epithet 'sage of Potiyil' names Agastya, and only the commentary makes Agastya the star here. The Lexicon's own headword பொதியில் (vol. V) gives only 'public hall' and the mountain, not the star, so this name is not lexicalised as an astronomical term.

entries.literal_meaning: the white one, the silver one (from veṇ-mai 'whiteness')
entries.usage_note: THE central Caṅkam sky-word. Venus quitting its proper station and moving to the southern quarter is the standard Tamil omen of drought and failed kingship; Puṟanāṉūṟu 35 makes the good king's land yield even so.
entries.citation: Puṟanāṉūṟu 35, ll. 6-7 (by Veḷḷaikkuṭi Nākaṉār, on Cōḻaṉ Kuḷamuṟṟattut Tuñciya Kiḷḷivaḷavaṉ); Project Madurai e-text PM 0057
entries.quote:
அலங்குகதிர்க் கனலி நால்வயின் தோன்றினும்,
இலங்குகதிர் வெள்ளி தென்புலம் படரினும்,
entries.notes: HOMONYM, and one the discipline requires flagging. The Tamil Lexicon (s.v. வெள்ளி¹, vol. VI p. 3794, https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/tamil-lex_query.py?qs=%E0%AE%B5%E0%AF%86%E0%AE%B3%E0%AF%8D%E0%AE%B3%E0%AE%BF&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact) prints ten senses on one headword: '1. Whiteness … 2. Silver, Argentum … 3. A silver coin … 4. Star; நட்சத்திரம் … 5. The planet Venus; சுக்கிரனென்னுங் கோள். இலங்கு கதிர் வெள்ளி தென்புலம் படரினும் (புறநா. 35) … 6. Śukra, the priest of the Asuras … 7. Friday … 9. Ignorance … 10. Semen virile.' Sense 1 is itself quoted from Puṟanāṉūṟu 41 and sense 7 from Cilappatikāram, so the word is ambiguous within the same corpus; the astronomical sense here is fixed by இலங்குகதிர் 'bright-rayed' and by the parallel with கனலி, the sun, in the preceding line. The Lexicon's ஊதுவாரம் (p. 496) makes the pun explicit: 'the Tamil word veḷḷi connoting the metal silver as well as the planet Venus'. Two further Puṟanāṉūṟu attestations of the same omen were verified in the same e-text: 388, l. 1 'வெள்ளி தென்புலத்து உறைய, விளைவயல் / பள்ளம், வாடிய பயன்இல் காலை' (Venus dwelling in the south, the fields withered), and 397, l. 1 'வெள்ளியும் இருவிசும்பு ஏர்தரும்' (Venus rising in the dark sky at dawn). No Sanskrit-database counterpart: the planets are not individually in that database.

entries.usage_note: The opening words of Paṭṭiṉappālai, and the same drought-omen as veḷḷi: 'even if the blameless-famed shining white star should turn from its quarter and go south'.
entries.citation: Paṭṭiṉappālai ll. 1-2 (by Kaṭiyalūr Uruttiraṅkaṇṇaṉār); Project Madurai e-text PM 0077
entries.quote:
வசையில்புகழ் வயங்குவெண்மீன்
திசைதிரிந்து தெற்கேகினும்
entries.notes: Nacciṉārkkiṉiyar's commentary on these lines glosses the phrase unambiguously: 'வயங்கு வெண்மீன் திசை திரிந்து தெற்கு ஏகினும் - விளங்குகின்ற வெள்ளியாகியமீன் தான் நிற்றற்குரிய வடதிசையினில்லாமல் தென்றிசைக்கண்ணே போகினும்' — 'the shining star that is Veḷḷi, even if it goes to the south instead of standing in its proper northern quarter' (U. Vē. Cāminātaiyar's edition, Project Madurai PM 0479, https://www.projectmadurai.org/pm_etexts/utf8/pmuni0479.html). The Tamil Lexicon (s.v. வெண்மீன், vol. VI p. 3782) glosses it 'Venus; சுக்கிரன்' and cites the line as பட்டினப். 14; the Project Madurai text and Nacciṉārkkiṉiyar's own numbering both place it at ll. 1-2, i.e. the poem's opening couplet, so the Lexicon's line-number appears to follow a different edition or is an error. Recorded as an edition discrepancy rather than silently corrected.

entries.literal_meaning: dawn-white, the white one of daybreak
entries.usage_note: The everyday modern Tamil name of the morning star, and the word the Lexicon uses to define all the others.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. விடிவெள்ளி, vol. VI p. 3659, marked (W.) after Winslow
entries.quote: விடிவெள்ளி viṭi-veḷḷi , n. < விடி² +. Venus, as the morning star; பின்னிரவில் தோன்றுஞ் சுக்கிரன். (W.)
entries.notes: Its poetic doublet is விடிமீன் viṭi-mīṉ 'dawn-star' (p. 3658, quoting Kallāṭam 17, 12, 'விடிமீன் முளைத்த தரளம்'), and its morning/evening pair is காலைவெள்ளி kālai-veḷḷi 'morning-white' (p. 900) against மாலைவெள்ளி mālai-veḷḷi 'evening-white' (p. 3179). All four are Tamil formations on veḷḷi.

entries.usage_note: The Caṅkam name for the morning star. In Akanāṉūṟu 17 the last silk-cotton blossoms scattered by the wind along a desert road are compared to it.
entries.citation: Akanāṉūṟu 17 (Pālai); text and commentary of Na. Mu. Vēṅkaṭacāmi Nāṭṭār, Project Madurai e-text PM 0490_01
entries.quote: வைகுறு மீனிற் றோன்று
entries.notes: Nāṭṭār's gloss in the same e-text reads 'வைகுறு மீனில் தோன்றும் - விடியற்காலத்தே வானத்தே காணப்படுகின்ற மீன் போன்று தோன்றுதற்கிடனான' — 'appearing like the star seen in the sky at dawn'. The Tamil Lexicon (s.v. வைகுறுமீன், vol. VI p. 3850) defines it 'Morning star; விடிவெள்ளி' and cites this line as அகநா. 17. Note that the verse itself says only 'the dawn star'; the equation with Venus specifically is the lexicographers'.

entries.literal_meaning: pure/refined silver; hence the morning star
entries.usage_note: A FOLK USE with a practical function: the Lexicon's illustrative sentence is a traveller's, 'The morning star has risen, so let us set out.' Marked Nāñ., i.e. the Nāñcilnāṭu dialect of the far south.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. சொக்கவெள்ளி sense 2, vol. III p. 1646, marked Nāñ.
entries.quote: சொக்கவெள்ளி cokka-veḷḷi , n. < சொக்கம்¹ +. 1. [K. cokkabeḷḷi, Tu. cokkaboḷḷi.] See சொக்கக்கட்டிவெள்ளி. Colloq. 2. Morning star; விடிவெள்ளி. சொக்கவெள்ளி உதயமாகிவிட்டதாற் புறப்படுவோம். Nāñ.
entries.notes: HOMONYM within the entry: sense 1, marked Colloq. and with Kannada and Tulu cognates, is refined silver bullion. The metal sense and the planet sense are the same metaphor running in two directions, which is exactly the veḷḷi trap. The star sense is fixed by the illustrative sentence — one does not set out on a journey because bullion has risen.

entries.usage_note: A nikaṇṭu word for the morning star, recorded from the Piṅkala Nikaṇṭu.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. வெடி⁴, vol. VI p. 3773, citing the Piṅkala Nikaṇṭu
entries.quote: வெடி⁴ veṭi , n. < வெடி³-. Venus, as the morning star; விடிவெள்ளி. (பிங்.)
entries.notes: SEVERE HOMONYM: வெடி² on the same page runs to nineteen senses — explosion, noise, thunder, gun, fireworks, fissure, hate, ruin, fear, incense, perfume, stench, toddy, a dice-play cant term, and (marked Nāñ.) 'big lie'. வெடி⁴ 'Venus' is a separate headword with a separate etymology, attested only in a lexicographical work, with no literary quotation. Confidence 'likely' on that account. Also on the same page வெடி⁵ = 'open plain'.

entries.usage_note: The evening-star half of the Tamil pair; the morning half is viṭiveḷḷi / kālaiveḷḷi.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. மாலைவெள்ளி, vol. V p. 3179, marked (W.) after Winslow
entries.quote: மாலைவெள்ளி mālai-veḷḷi , n. < id. +. Venus, when it appears as the evening star; அந்தியிற்றோன்றும் சுக்கிரன். (W.)
entries.notes: Only two Tamil words for the evening star are in the Lexicon: this one and the Sanskrit-based அந்திநட்சத்திரம் anti-naṭcattiram (p. 83), 'Evening star; மாலைவெள்ளி'. The morning star, by contrast, has at least eight Tamil names — an asymmetry worth noting: the Tamil sky-vocabulary is a dawn vocabulary.

entries.usage_note: Named by colour, like veṇmīṉ 'white star' for Venus and cemmīṉ 'red star'. The Puṟanāṉūṟu line stacks three portents — the black star smoking, a comet appearing, Venus running to the south — and says the good king's land is watered even so.
entries.citation: Puṟanāṉūṟu 117, ll. 1-2 (by Kapilar); Project Madurai e-text PM 0057
entries.quote:
மைம் மீன் புகையினும், தூமம் தோன்றினும்,
தென் திசை மருங்கின் வெள்ளி ஓடினும்,
entries.notes: The Tamil Lexicon (s.v. மைம்மீன், vol. V p. 3369, https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/tamil-lex_query.py?qs=%E0%AE%AE%E0%AF%88%E0%AE%AE%E0%AF%8D%E0%AE%AE%E0%AF%80%E0%AE%A9%E0%AF%8D&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact) defines it 'The planet Saturn, as black in colour; சனி' and cites this line as புறநா. 117. This one couplet is the single richest Tamil astronomical line: it gives maimmīṉ (Saturn), tūmam (comet) and veḷḷi (Venus) in two lines, all three as omens of drought. No Sanskrit-database counterpart; the planets are not individually in that database.

entries.usage_note: A TAMIL NAME WITH NO SANSKRIT MODEL: the galaxy as a smudge on the sky, not as a celestial river. Every Sanskrit name for the Milky Way is a Ganges-metaphor; this one is not.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. மாசு¹ sense 11, vol. V p. 3147, marked (W.) after Winslow
entries.quote: மாசு¹ mācu , n. … 1. Spot; மறு. … 2. Stain, taint, tarnish; அழுக்கு. … 5. Blackness; கருமை. … 7. Cloud; மேகம். (பிங்.) … 11. The Milky Way; பால்வீதிமண்டலம். (W.)
entries.notes: HOMONYM-HEAVY: eighteen senses on one headword, including ordure, bile, phlegm, afterbirth and a film in the eye. Only sense 11 is astronomical, and it is Winslow's; Winslow's own entry reads 'The galaxy, or milky way, பால்வீதிமண்டலம்' (1862, p. 859, https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/winslow_query.py?qs=Milky+Way&matchtype=default). No literary attestation in the astronomical sense was found, but the sense is confirmed by the compound pūrāṭa-mācu below. sanskrit_db_id given as the Milky Way entry akashaganga on referent identity only — the name itself has no Sanskrit counterpart.

entries.literal_meaning: the Pūrāṭam stain — the smudge at the twentieth asterism
entries.usage_note: The galaxy named for the part of the zodiac where it is brightest. Pūrāṭam is Pūrvāṣāḍhā, in Sagittarius — which is where the Milky Way's central bulge lies. The name is an accurate piece of sky-description.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. பூராடமாசு, vol. V p. 2847, marked (W.) after Winslow
entries.quote: பூராடமாசு pūrāṭa-mācu , n. < id. +. Galaxy, the Milky Way; பால்வீதிமண்டலம். (W.)
entries.notes: Winslow's own entry, s.v. பூராடம் (1862, p. 808), reads 'பூராடமாசு, s. The galaxy or milky way, பால்வீதிமண்டலம்; (adopted.)' — his '(adopted)' means the term is taken up rather than native to his colloquial register. That the Milky Way should be named for Pūrvāṣāḍhā rather than for any other asterism is not accidental and is not, as far as this compilation found, paralleled in Sanskrit.

entries.usage_note: The standard Tamil astronomical term, and the word by which the Lexicon defines every other Milky Way name. The Lexicon marks it '(Astron.)' and glosses it with the Latin via lactea.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. பால்வீதிமண்டலம், vol. V p. 2628, marked (W.) after Winslow
entries.quote: பால்வீதிமண்டலம் pāl-vīti-maṇṭalam , n. < id. + வீதி +. (Astron.) Milky Way, via lactea; வானத்தின் ஒருபுறமாக நீளத்தோன்றும் நட்சத்திரத்திரளின் ஒளி. (W.)
entries.notes: The elements pāl 'milk' and maṇṭalam are Tamil and Sanskrit respectively, vīti < Skt. vīthī 'street'; the compound as a whole is a Tamil formation. Because the Lexicon glosses it with via lactea and attributes it to Winslow, a European calque cannot be ruled out — but the Tamil definition, 'the light of the mass of stars appearing lengthwise along one side of the sky', is descriptive rather than mythological, unlike the Sanskrit names. No literary attestation found.

entries.usage_note: Sanskrit Ākāśagaṅgā in Tamil phonology; the whole Ganges-in-the-sky family enters Tamil intact.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. ஆகாசகங்கை, vol. I p. 205
entries.quote: *ஆகாசகங்கை ākāca-kaṅkai , n. < id. +. 1. The celestial Ganges; மந்தாகினி. 2. The Milky Way; பால்வீதிமண்டலம்.
entries.notes: Its Tamil companions in the same family are மந்தாகினி mantākiṉi (p. 3066, = Skt. Mandākinī, Sanskrit-database id mandakini), விண்டுநதி viṇṭu-nati 'Viṣṇu's river' (p. 3664, from the Yāḻppāṇa Akarāti), அமராபகை amarāpakai (Supplement p. S051, quoted from the Cintāmaṇi commentary) and சித்தகங்கை citta-kaṅkai 'the Siddhas' Ganges' (Supplement p. S274).

entries.usage_note: A SEMANTIC DIVERGENCE worth recording. The word is Sanskrit Nāgavīthī, but in Tamil lexicography it denotes the Milky Way, whereas in the Sanskrit tradition Nāgavīthī is one of the nine star-roads (vīthī) of the ecliptic belt, not the galaxy at all.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. நாகவீதி, vol. IV p. 2200, citing the Yāḻppāṇa Akarāti
entries.quote: நாகவீதி nāka-vīti , n. < nāka + vīthī. Milky Way; பால்வீதிமண்டலம். (யாழ். அக.)
entries.notes: Marked disputed because the Tamil gloss contradicts the Sanskrit database entry 'nagavithi' (the Serpent-road, northernmost of the nine star-roads, a segment of the ecliptic belt). Either the Yāḻppāṇa Akarāti has confused vīthī 'road' with the pāl-vīti 'milk-street' of the galaxy, or a genuine Tamil re-application has occurred. The Lexicon's நட்சத்திரவீதி naṭcattira-vīti (p. 2135) shows the same slide, glossing it both '1. Moon's path in the zodiac' and '2. The Milky Way'. A caution for anyone joining the two databases on this id.

entries.usage_note: An opaque Tamil name for the galaxy recorded only from the Yāḻppāṇa Akarāti; the Lexicon itself will not commit to an etymology.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. மணலக்கம்பம், vol. V p. 3038, citing the Yāḻppāṇa Akarāti
entries.quote: மணலக்கம்பம் maṇalakkampam , n. perh. மணல் + lakṣa + பம். The Milky Way; பால்வீதிமண்டலம். (யாழ். அக.)
entries.notes: The Lexicon's etymology is prefixed 'perh.' and parses it as maṇal 'sand' + Skt. lakṣa 'lakh' + an unexplained -pam — i.e. something like 'a hundred thousand grains of sand', which would be a fine name for the Milky Way but is expressly a guess. Recorded with the guess flagged as the Lexicon flags it. Confidence 'likely' for the referent (the definition is unambiguous), not for the etymology.

entries.usage_note: The living Tamil word for a comet, formed on vāl 'tail' + mīṉ 'star'; வால்நட்சத்திரம் vāl-naṭcattiram is the same compound with the Sanskrit word for star, and is the commoner modern form.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. வால்மீன், vol. VI p. 3616, marked (W.) after Winslow; and s.v. வான்மீன்², p. 3626, citing the Piṅkala Nikaṇṭu
entries.quote: வால்மீன் vāl-mīṉ , n. < வால்² + மீன்¹. See வால்நட்சத்திரம். (W.)
entries.notes: HOMONYM CAUTION: the variant spelling வான்மீன்² vāṉ-mīṉ (p. 3626) is also 'comet' — the Lexicon derives it from வால் 'tail', not from வான் 'sky' — and sits immediately beside வான்மீன்¹ vāṉ-mīṉ 'star' from வான் 'sky'. Two identical spellings, opposite senses, one page. The head entry வால்நட்சத்திரம் is at p. 3615. Also in the family: வானட்சத்திரம் (p. 3626, Yāḻppāṇa Akarāti) and பாலநக்ஷத்திரம் (p. 2629).

entries.usage_note: The Caṅkam word for a comet as a portent, in the Puṟanāṉūṟu omen-triad beside Saturn and Venus.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. தூமம் sense 6, vol. IV p. 2018; quoting Puṟanāṉūṟu 117
entries.quote: 6. See தூமகேது. தூமந் தோன்றினும் (புறநா. 117).
entries.notes: The Puṟanāṉūṟu 117 line was verified independently in the Project Madurai e-text (PM 0057, https://www.projectmadurai.org/pm_etexts/utf8/pmuni0057.html): 'மைம் மீன் புகையினும், தூமம் தோன்றினும்,'. HOMONYM: the same headword's senses 1-5 are smoke, perfume, censer, an astrological term, and a potter's kiln; sense 6 alone is the comet. The full form is தூமகேது tūma-kētu (p. 2018), 'Comet, one of four karantuṟaikōḷ' — 'the four hidden-and-appearing bodies', a Tamil classification of transient sky-objects.

entries.usage_note: A Tamil formation for a comet, from the Cilappatikāram's list of portents; the metaphor is a banner or creeper of smoke rather than a tailed star.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. புகைக்கொடி, vol. V p. 2743; quoting the aruñcolpporuḷ on Cilappatikāram 20, 102
entries.quote: புகைக்கொடி pukai-k-koṭi , n. < id. +. Comet; தூமகேது. புகைக்கொடி தோன்றினும் (சிலப். 20, 102, அரும்.).
entries.notes: Its twin is கனற்கொடி kaṉaṟ-koṭi 'fire-banner' (Supplement p. S211, quoting Takkayākapparaṇi 457), also 'comet'. The Takkayākapparaṇi commentary at that same verse yields a small Tamil vocabulary of comet-types — அராளகி arāḷaki, அவ்வியக்தி avviyakti, அவீசி avīci (Supplement pp. S062, S071, S076), each glossed 'a kind of comet' — a classification the Lexicon does not further explain and which is not pursued here.

entries.usage_note: The standard Tamil term for a meteor, and the word the Lexicon uses to define the Sanskrit uṟkam and tūmakētu. Entirely Tamil in its elements.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. விண்வீழ்கொள்ளி, vol. VI p. 3666, citing the Cūṭāmaṇi Nikaṇṭu
entries.quote: விண்வீழ்கொள்ளி viṇ-vīḻ-koḷḷi , n. < விண்¹ + வீழ்- +. Meteor; shooting star; விண்ணினின்று விழும் நட்சத்திரம்போன்ற சுடர். (சூடா.)
entries.notes: The Tamil definition is careful — 'a light like a star, falling from the sky' — i.e. Tamil lexicography distinguishes the meteor from a star proper. The Sanskrit-derived equivalents in Tamil are உற்கம் uṟkam (p. 478, < ulkā) and ஆகாசபலம் ākāca-palam (p. 205).

entries.usage_note: The -mīṉ form of the same idea, and the one attested in the commentary tradition on the Tolkāppiyam.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. வீழ்மீன், vol. VI p. 3762; quoting the commentary on Tolkāppiyam, Poruḷatikāram 91
entries.quote: வீழ்மீன் vīḻ-mīṉ , n. < id. + மீன்¹. Meteor; விண்வீழ்கொள்ளி. (தொல். பொ. 91, உரை.)
entries.notes: The variant விழுமீன்¹ viḻu-mīṉ (p. 3723) is glossed 'Meteor. See வீழ்மீன்' — and immediately beside it விழுமீன்² is the hilsa fish, one more mīṉ homonym. The citation is to the commentary on the Tolkāppiyam, not to the sūtra itself: the mūlam of the Tolkāppiyam names no sky-object, as recorded in summary_findings.

entries.sky_object: Mṛgaśīrṣa, the fifth nakshatra (the head of Orion)
entries.usage_note: A Tamil counting-name, from மூ 'three', for the asterism the Sanskrit tradition calls 'the deer's head'. Recorded by the Tivākaram, the oldest surviving Tamil glossary.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. மும்மீன், vol. V p. 3272, citing the Tivākaram
entries.quote: மும்மீன் mu-m-mīṉ , n. < id. + மீன்¹. The fifth nakṣatra. See மிருகசீருடம். (திவா.)
entries.notes: CAUTION against a natural misreading: 'three stars' in Orion suggests the Belt to a modern eye, but the fifth nakṣatra is the head-group λ, φ¹, φ² Orionis, and the Tamil Lexicon refers the word to மிருகசீருடம் (p. 3201, < Skt. mṛga-śīrṣa). Winslow independently describes the mansion as 'containing three stars in Orion, and figured by an antelope's head' (1862, s.v. மிருகம், p. 869) — the same three stars, the head not the belt. NEGATIVE FINDING: no Tamil name for Orion's Belt as a separate figure was found in either lexicon. The Lexicon's other name for the fifth nakṣatra is மதிநாள் mati-nāḷ 'moon-star' (p. 3057, Piṅkala Nikaṇṭu), Soma being its presiding deity.

entries.literal_meaning: holy Ātirai (Skt. ārdrā), with the Tamil honorific tiru-
entries.usage_note: The only Tamil word the Lexicon's English side returns for a search on 'Orion'. It is the Sanskrit Ārdrā with the Tamil honorific prefixed, and it carries a Śaiva festival and a girl's pre-marriage rite with it.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. திருவாதிரை, vol. IV p. 1917, citing the Piṅkala Nikaṇṭu
entries.quote: திருவாதிரை tiru-v-ātirai , n. < id. + ārdrā. 1. The 6th nakṣatra, part of Orion; ஆறாவது நட்சத்திரம். (பிங்.) 2. A festival in the month of Mārkaḻi. See ஆருத்திராதரிசனம். 3. A special ceremony observed on the day of āruttirā-taricaṉam before a girl's marriage when she is given a bath and decorated … Nāṭ. Cheṭṭi. (E. T. v, 264.)
entries.notes: ETHNOGRAPHIC CROSS-REFERENCE: sense 3 is sourced by the Lexicon to 'E. T. v, 264' — Edgar Thurston, Castes and Tribes of Southern India, vol. V — and attributed to the Nāṭṭukkōṭṭai Chettis. This is the Tamil Lexicon itself citing the ethnography, and is the only place in this compilation where a star-derived Tamil term is anchored to a named community practice. Sense 2 is the Mārkaḻi Ārudrā-darśana festival. See also the disputed reading of செம்மீன் above, where an old commentary makes Puṟanāṉūṟu 60's 'red star' this asterism.

entries.usage_note: A Tamil counting-name from ஐ 'five', and the Lexicon states the reason: the asterism has five principal stars — the quadrilateral of Corvus with its fifth.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. ஐம்மீன், vol. I p. 579, citing the Piṅkala Nikaṇṭu
entries.quote: ஐம்மீன் ai-m-mīṉ , n. < id. +. 1. The 13th nakṣatra, so called because of its five principal stars. See அத்தம்⁸. (பிங்.) 2. The fourth nakṣatra. See உரோகிணி. (வீமேசுர. 15.)
entries.notes: Sense 2, 'the fourth nakṣatra' = Rohiṇī, comes from a different source and reflects the five bright Hyades; the Lexicon prints both without adjudicating, so the counting-name is genuinely ambiguous between two five-star groups. Its calque-twin is கைம்மீன் kai-m-mīṉ 'hand-star' (p. 1112, Tivākaram), a straight Tamil translation of Sanskrit hasta 'hand'. The Lexicon locates the thirteenth s.v. அத்தம்⁸ (p. 65) as 'the constellation Corvus'.

entries.literal_meaning: last star, the star at the end
entries.usage_note: A positional Tamil name — Revatī named simply as the last of the twenty-seven. It pairs with ātimīṉ and talaināḷ, 'first star', for Aśvinī.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. கடைமீன், vol. II p. 680, citing the Tivākaram
entries.quote: கடைமீன் kaṭai-mīṉ , n. < id. +. The 27th nakṣatra from its being the last of the asterisms. See இரேவதி. (திவா.)
entries.notes: Its -nāḷ counterpart is கடைநாள் kaṭai-nāḷ (p. 679, Cūṭāmaṇi Nikaṇṭu), sense 4, 'the 27th nakṣatra, from its being the last asterism' — whose senses 1-3 are 'the last day', 'the day of one's death' and 'the last day of the world', a homonym worth noting. Further Tamil names for the same asterism: பெருநாள் peru-nāḷ (p. 2877) and புருடநாள் puruṭa-nāḷ (p. 2775); the Sanskritic one is இரவிநாள் iravi-nāḷ 'sun-star' (p. 316).

entries.literal_meaning: physician-star, the star of the physicians
entries.usage_note: A Tamil TRANSLATION of the deity rather than a borrowing of the name: the Aśvins are the physicians of the gods, and Tamil renders them with the native word maruttuvar 'physicians'.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. மருத்துவநாள், vol. V p. 3092, citing the Piṅkala Nikaṇṭu
entries.quote: மருத்துவநாள் maruttuva-nāḷ , n. < மருத்துவர் +. The first nakṣatra; அச்சுவினி நாள். (பிங்.)
entries.notes: The same asterism also has the positional Tamil names தலைநாள் talai-nāḷ 'head-day, first star' (p. 1780, Piṅkala Nikaṇṭu) and ஆதிமீன் āti-mīṉ 'first star' (p. 229, quoting Cētupurāṇam, Kantamātaṉa 17: 'ஆதிமீன் றோணி யீறு'), and the fully Sanskritic ஐப்பசி (see the month entry). The Sanskrit-database counterpart naming the same idea is 'ashvinidaivata'.

modern_star.bayer: α, θ¹, θ², γ, δ, ε Tauri

entries.usage_note: The V of the Hyades seen as a bullock-cart. Sanskrit śakaṭa in Tamil form, but the figure itself is the shared South Asian one; the Tamil Lexicon lists the asterism sense among the ordinary cart senses without comment.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. சகடம்¹ sense 4, vol. III p. 1255, citing the Piṅkala Nikaṇṭu
entries.quote: சகடம்¹ cakaṭam , n. < šakaṭa. 1. Cart, wheeled conveyance drawn by cattle, carriage, chariot; வண்டி. … 4. The 4th nakṣatra. See உரோகிணி. (பிங்.) 5. Wheel; சக்கரம்.
entries.notes: Corresponds directly to the Sanskrit-database entry rohini-shakata, 'the Wain of Rohiṇī'. HOMONYM: five separate சகடம் headwords — a large drum, a sparrow, a cup, and a carambola tree — of which only சகடம்¹ sense 4 is astronomical. The purely Tamil name for the same asterism is வயமீன் vaya-mīṉ (p. 3496), which the Lexicon derives only tentatively ('prob. வயம்⁵ + மீன்¹') and glosses 'The fourth nakṣatra; உரோகணி'.

entries.usage_note: A TAMIL NAME WITH NO SANSKRIT MODEL: Citrā named purely by its position, the fourteenth of twenty-seven, the exact midpoint of the series. Nothing about the deity or the appearance enters into it.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. நடுநாள் sense 3, vol. IV p. 2143, citing the Cūṭāmaṇi Nikaṇṭu
entries.quote: நடுநாள் naṭu-nāḷ , n. < id. +. 1. Midday; நண்பகல். 2. Midnight; இடையாமம். பழவிறன் மூதூர் பாயல்கொ ணடுநாள் (மணி. 7, 63). 3. The 14th nakṣatra. See சித்திரை. (சூடா.)
entries.notes: HOMONYM: senses 1 and 2 of the same word are 'midday' and 'midnight' — 'the middle of the day' and 'the middle asterism' share one form, and the Maṇimēkalai citation belongs to the midnight sense. The pun is presumably deliberate on the nikaṇṭu-maker's part. The bare word மீன் mīṉ is also given for this asterism (s.v. மீன்¹ sense 2), as is நெய்வான்மீன் ney-vāṉ-mīṉ (p. 2343, Tivākaram), whose first element is opaque.

entries.usage_note: The only Tamil word the Lexicon's English side returns for a search on 'Arcturus'. A Tamil translation of the Sanskrit Vāyavya: the Wind-god's asterism, rendered with the ordinary Tamil word for wind.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. காற்றினாள், vol. II p. 909, citing the Piṅkala Nikaṇṭu
entries.quote: காற்றினாள் kāṟṟiṉāḷ , n. < id. + நாள். Svātī, the 15th nakṣatra, as having Wind-god for its presiding deity, Arcturus; வாயுவைத் தேவதையாகக் கொண்ட சுவாதிநாள். (பிங்.)
entries.notes: The Lexicon spells out the modern identification, 'Arcturus', which the Sanskrit database also gives for Svātī. Its half-borrowed rival is அனிலநாள் aṉila-nāḷ (p. 191, < Skt. anila 'wind' + Tamil nāḷ, Tivākaram). The corresponding Sanskrit-database entry is pavana-svati, 'Pavana / Anila / Vāyavya'.

entries.literal_meaning: the star that the wind-star precedes
entries.usage_note: THE PUREST VERNACULAR FORMATION IN THIS FILE. Viśākhā is named neither by its deity nor by its shape but purely by its place in the Tamil sequence — the asterism that comes after kāṟṟiṉāḷ. Nothing in Sanskrit corresponds.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. காற்றுமுந்துநாள், vol. II p. 909, citing the Cūṭāmaṇi Nikaṇṭu
entries.quote: காற்றுமுந்துநாள் kāṟṟu-muntu-nāḷ , n. < id. +. Višākha, the 16th nakṣatra, as succeeding kāṟṟiṉāḷ; காற்றைத் தேவதையாகக்கொண்ட சுவாதியை முற்பட்டநாளாகவுடைய விசாகநட்சத்திரம். (சூடா.)
entries.notes: Printed immediately after காற்றினாள் on the same Lexicon page, which is how the relation is meant to be read. The formation presupposes a fixed Tamil ordering of the asterisms in which position alone can name a star — evidence that the Tamil nakshatra sequence was learned as a Tamil list, not merely translated item by item.

entries.literal_meaning: water-star, the star of the waters
entries.usage_note: A Tamil translation of the deity — Pūrvāṣāḍhā's presiding power is the Waters (Āpas) — with the native word nīr.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. நீர்நாள், vol. IV p. 2303, citing the Piṅkala Nikaṇṭu
entries.quote: நீர்நாள் nīr-nāḷ , n. < id. +. The 20th nakṣatra. See பூராடம். (பிங்.)
entries.notes: The Tamil deity-translation habit runs right through: கடல் kaṭal 'sea' is given as the 24th nakṣatra Catayam, 'so called from Varuṇa the Sea-god being the deity of the constellation' (p. 660); அசுரநாள் acura-nāḷ is Mūlam (p. 33); தருமநாள் taruma-nāḷ is Paraṇi (p. 1770); மித்திரநாள் mittira-nāḷ is Anuṭam (p. 3198); விசுவநாள் vicuva-nāḷ is Uttirāṭam (p. 3646); குருநாள் kuru-nāḷ and சுரர்குருநாள் curar-kuru-nāḷ 'the star of the gods' preceptor' are Pūcam (pp. 1017, 1526); அதிதிநாள் atiti-nāḷ is Puṉarpūcam (p. 74); பகவதிநாள் pakavati-nāḷ is Pūram (p. 2382); இசைநாள் icai-nāḷ is Pūraṭṭāti and Uttiraṭṭāti (p. 273).

entries.literal_meaning: rain-star, the star of the rains
entries.usage_note: An AGRICULTURAL star-name: the twelfth asterism named for the rain. It is the only asterism in the Lexicon named for a season rather than a deity, a shape or a number.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. மாரிநாள், vol. V p. 3173, citing the Piṅkala Nikaṇṭu
entries.quote: மாரிநாள் māri-nāḷ , n. < மாரி¹ +. The 12th nakṣatra. See உத்தரம்². (பிங்.)
entries.notes: The Lexicon gives no reason for the name, so the agricultural reading is an inference from the transparent meaning of māri 'rain, rainy season' — flagged as such, and confidence set to 'likely' for that reason. The same asterism's other Tamil names are கதிர்நாள் katir-nāḷ (p. 713) and செங்கதிர்நாள் ceṅ-katir-nāḷ (p. 1578), both 'sun-ray star', which the Lexicon does explain: 'whose presiding deity is the Sun'.

entries.sky_object: Magha, the tenth nakshatra (the Sickle of Leo)
entries.usage_note: THE ONE INDIGENOUS CONSTELLATION-FIGURE recovered by this compilation. Nacciṉārkkiṉiyar, glossing this compound, says the Magha asterism 'has the shape of a bent yoke' — the Sickle of Leo seen as a crooked ox-yoke, which is why the poet uses it as a simile for the curving bank of a temple tank.
entries.citation: Paṭṭiṉappālai ll. 34-35, with Nacciṉārkkiṉiyar's commentary (ed. U. Vē. Cāminātaiyar); Project Madurai e-text PM 0479
entries.quote: (கு -பு) மகவெண்மீன் - மகநக்ஷத்திரம்; அது முடநுகம்போன்ற வடிவமுடையதாதலின், கரைக்கு உவமையாயிற்று.
entries.notes: The mūlam lines were verified separately in the plain e-text (PM 0077, https://www.projectmadurai.org/pm_etexts/utf8/pmuni0077.html): 'மழைநீங்கிய மாவிசும்பின் / மதிசேர்ந்த மகவெண்மீன்' — 'in the great sky from which the rain has withdrawn, the Magha white-star joined to the moon'. Nacciṉārkkiṉiyar's running gloss on ll. 34-38 renders it 'மதியைச் சேர்ந்த மகமாகிய வெள்ளியமீனினது வடிவு' — 'the shape of the white star that is Magha, joined to the moon'. முடநுகம் muṭa-nukam is 'bent yoke'. The Sickle of Leo — α, η, γ, ζ, μ, ε Leonis — does form a hooked line answering to a yoke, and the figure is not the Sanskrit one (Sanskrit Maghā is a house or a whip). The compound is not a Tamil Lexicon headword; it exists only in this text and its commentary, which is why the citation is literary rather than lexicographical. HOMONYM caution: வெண்மீன் alone means Venus (see above); here மக- fixes it as the asterism.

entries.sky_object: the seventh Tamil month, named for Aśvinī
entries.literal_meaning: from Skt. āśvayuj, 'joined to the Aśvins'
entries.usage_note: One of the twelve Tamil month-names still in daily use, all of them asterism-derived. The Lexicon records that the word also names the asterism itself.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. ஐப்பசி, vol. I p. 578; quoting Cīvakacintāmaṇi 1770
entries.quote: ஐப்பசி aippaci , n. < āšvayuj. 1. The seventh Tamil month, October-November; ஏழாவது மாதம். (உபதேசரத். 6.) 2. The first nakṣstra. See அசுவதி. (சீவக. 1770.)
entries.notes: The Lexicon's derivations for the rest of the twelve, all verified at the same endpoint: சித்திரை Cittirai < citrā (p. 1391), வைகாசி Vaikāci < vaiśākha (p. 3849), ஆடி Āṭi < āṣāḍha (p. 219), ஆவணி Āvaṇi < śrāvaṇa (p. 249), புரட்டாசி Puraṭṭāci cf. proṣṭhapadā (p. 2769), கார்த்திகை Kārttikai < kṛttikā (p. 880), மார்கழி Mārkaḻi < mārgaśīrṣa (p. 3170), தை Tai < taiṣī (p. 2074), மாசி Māci < māgha (p. 3147), பங்குனி Paṅkuṉi < Pkt. phagguṇi < phalgunī (p. 2390). ஆனி Āṉi (p. 221) is the exception: the Lexicon gives it NO etymology at all, while recording that it also names the 19th nakṣatra (Mūlam) and the 21st (Uttirāṭam) — a gap worth flagging.

entries.sky_object: the eleventh Tamil month, named for Magha
entries.literal_meaning: from Skt. māgha, the month of the Magha asterism
entries.usage_note: The one Tamil month-name attested by name in the Caṅkam corpus itself, described there by its astronomical property: the month in which the day does not lengthen and the night grows.
entries.citation: Patiṟṟuppattu 59, ll. 1-2 (Sixth Ten); Project Madurai e-text PM 0038
entries.quote:
பகல்நீ(டு) ஆகா(து) இரவுப்பொழுது பெருகி
மாசி நின்ற மாகூர் திங்கள்
entries.notes: TEXTUAL NOTE: the Project Madurai e-text prints line 2 as 'மாசி நின்ற *மாகூர் திங்கள்*', the asterisks and bold flanking மாகூர் திங்கள் because that phrase is this poem's பெயர் (title-phrase), given as such in its colophon — they are editorial emphasis, not a lacuna, and the line is continuous. Line 1's '(டு)' and '(து)' are the editor's parenthesised restorations and are kept here as printed; nothing has been supplied by the compiler. The Tamil Lexicon (s.v. மாசி², vol. V p. 3147) cites this exact line as பதிற்றுப். 59, 2 and defines the word 'The 11th solar month = February-March', adding sense 2, 'The 10th nakṣatra. See மகம்²', from the commentary on Cilappatikāram 3, 123. HOMONYM: மாசி¹ on the previous page is 'mist, cloud' and 'a sea-fish', probably from மாசு.

entries.sky_object: the north-east monsoon squall of the month named for Aśvinī
entries.usage_note: A WEATHER TERM keyed to an asterism-named month — the practical end of the Tamil star-calendar, matching āṟāmīṉ-aṟavōṭṭu among the seamen.
entries.citation: Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924-36), s.v. ஐப்பசிக்குழப்பம், vol. I p. 578, marked (J.)
entries.quote: ஐப்பசிக்குழப்பம் aippaci-k-kuḻappam , n. < ஐப்பசி +. Rough weather at the setting in of the north-east monsoon in October; ஐப்பசிமாதத்தில் தோன்றுகிற புயல். (J.)
entries.notes: Aippaci and the Pleiades passage of āṟāmīṉ-aṟavōṭṭu mark the same weather from two directions — the month named for the first asterism and the sun's transit of the third. Together they are the whole of the agricultural and maritime star-calendar recoverable from these lexica; nothing more specific (sowing-stars, harvest-stars, named navigation stars) was found in the Tamil Lexicon, Winslow, or in Thurston's Castes and Tribes of Southern India.

caveats: LINKING RULE for sanskrit_db_id: the id links on REFERENT identity, i.e. it points to the entry in docs/star-names/star-names.json that denotes the same sky object, choosing the closest-matching Sanskrit name where several exist. It does NOT assert that the Tamil name is a borrowing or a translation of that Sanskrit name — for the vernacular entries (aṟumīṉ, eḻumīṉ, naṭunāḷ, kāṟṟumuntunāḷ, mācu and the rest) it is precisely the point that no Sanskrit counterpart name exists. Where the Tamil name IS the Sanskrit name in Tamil phonology, the notes say so. Planets have no ids because the Sanskrit database does not carry them individually.

The Tamil Lexicon prints its sources as Tamil sigla whose expansions are in front matter that survives on DSAL only as scanned images without a text layer. The sigla used in this file are expanded as: பிங். = Piṅkala Nikaṇṭu, திவா. = Tivākaram, சூடா. = Cūṭāmaṇi Nikaṇṭu, யாழ். அக. = Yāḻppāṇa Akarāti, (W.) = Winslow's dictionary. These four nikaṇṭu identifications are corroborated from the Lexicon's own headwords பிங்கலம், திவாகரம், சூடாமணிநிகண்டு and நிகண்டு, which describe each work. The regional labels Pond., Nāñ., Loc., Colloq. and (J.) are quoted as printed and their expansions are not asserted beyond what the entries themselves show.

Every Caṅkam quotation was read in a Project Madurai UTF-8 e-text that was actually fetched, and every Tamil Lexicon and Winslow quotation was read at the DSAL query URL given. Nothing has been transcribed from memory, back-transliterated, or normalised. Where a text prints editorial asterisks, brackets or restorations (Patiṟṟuppattu 59, Akanāṉūṟu 17), the entry says so.

Project Madurai e-texts are volunteer transcriptions of printed editions and carry occasional typographic damage; a few characters in the Paripāṭal file are corrupted. All lines quoted here were checked for legibility, but they are not a critical edition and line-numbering follows the file's own markers where these exist.

One line-number discrepancy is recorded rather than resolved: the Tamil Lexicon cites veṇmīṉ at Paṭṭiṉappālai 14, while both the Project Madurai plain text and Nacciṉārkkiṉiyar's own numbering in U. Vē. Cāminātaiyar's edition put it at lines 1-2, the poem's opening couplet.
Caṅkam dating is contested. The 'c. 1st-3rd c. CE' and similar ranges in source_date are conventional and approximate; nothing in this file depends on them.

The identifications of Caṅkam star-words with particular modern objects are the Tamil Lexicon's and the mediaeval commentators', not the poems'. The verses generally say 'the white star', 'the red star', 'the northern star'; it is Nacciṉārkkiṉiyar and the nineteenth- and twentieth-century lexicographers who say Venus, Mars, Arundhatī. Entries where this matters are marked 'likely' or 'disputed' and the reasoning is in the notes.

The mīṉ / mīṉ 'star' / 'fish' homonymy is systematic and dangerous: a large majority of Tamil Lexicon headwords ending in -mīṉ are fish. Every -mīṉ entry in this file was taken from a headword whose printed definition is astronomical, and the notes flag the fish-homonym wherever the same spelling carries one (ciṟumīṉ, viḻumīṉ, cemmīṉ, vāṉmīṉ). The parallel veḷḷi 'silver / whiteness / Friday / Venus' trap is flagged on every veḷḷi entry.

Edgar Thurston's Castes and Tribes of Southern India (1909), all seven volumes searched in full text on archive.org, yielded almost nothing for Tamil vernacular star-names: what star material it has is Brahmanical marriage ritual (the showing of Dhruva and Arundhatī), nakshatra-matching for marriages, and festival dates. The one substantive Tamil item — the Nāṭṭukkōṭṭai Chetti Ārudrā rite — reaches this file through the Tamil Lexicon's own citation of Thurston vol. V p. 264, not through a passage located directly. No community-specific Tamil sky-lore of the kind the sources were searched for was found there.

Fabricius's Tamil and English Dictionary (4th ed., 1972) IS on DSAL — this file previously said it was not — and was searched on a later correction pass. It adds no name to this file and confirms its negatives: 'Sirius', 'Antares', 'Arcturus' and 'Canopus' return nothing at all in full-text search, so the absence of Tamil names for those four stars now rests on three independent dictionaries rather than two. Its one novelty is rejected: at s.v. நட்சத்திரம் (p. 584) Fabricius glosses நட்சத்திரமாலை naṭcattira-mālai as 'the galaxy or milky way', where the Madras Tamil Lexicon (p. 2135) gives the word only as a cluster of stars, as the lunar zodiac of twenty-seven asterisms, as a synonym of நட்சத்திரவீதி the moon's path, and as the title of a treatise — no Milky Way sense anywhere. Fabricius is a Tamil-English dictionary made for missionaries and the gloss looks like his own; no entry is claimed on it. Winslow (1862) was consulted throughout and is quoted or cited where it adds colloquial evidence the Tamil Lexicon lacks.

Modern scholarship on Tamil astronomy and on Caṅkam chronology is in copyright and has not been quoted anywhere in this file; no in-copyright translation of any Caṅkam poem has been used, and the English renderings that appear in usage_note fields are the compiler's own working paraphrases, offered as orientation and not as translations of record.

This is a lexicographical and literary compilation, not a field survey. Living folk and fishermen's star-names in coastal Tamil Nadu, and any tribal astronomies of the Nilgiris or the Western Ghats, are almost certainly richer than what two nineteenth- and twentieth-century dictionaries preserve; no entry in this file is tagged 'tribal' because no citable tribal Tamil star-name was found in the sources searched.
